detail:
MedlinePlus describes gout as a form of arthritis caused by a buildup of uric acid in the body. When uric acid levels stay high, needle-like urate crystals can form in and around a joint, triggering sudden episodes of intense inflammation. The joint at the base of the big toe is the most commonly affected, although ankles, knees, elbows, wrists, and fingers can also be involved.

MedlinePlus notes that a gout flare can include sudden, severe joint pain, swelling, redness, warmth, and tenderness, often beginning at night, with symptoms peaking and then easing over days to a week or more. Between flares, a person may have no symptoms, although untreated buildup can lead to more frequent flares, deposits of crystals called tophi, and joint damage over time. Clinicians usually diagnose gout using medical history and examination, blood tests for uric acid, imaging in some cases, and, when confirmation is needed, examination of fluid drawn from an affected joint for urate crystals.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about gout symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: MedlinePlus describes gout as arthritis caused by uric acid buildup and urate crystal formation in joints, producing sudden flares of severe pain, swelling, and redness most often in the big toe.
takeaways: gout results from urate crystals forming in and around joints
symptoms can include sudden severe pain, swelling, redness, and warmth
joint fluid examination can confirm crystals when diagnosis is uncertain
title: Gout: when uric acid crystals trigger sudden joint inflammation
